purpose: Verified, job-specific accomplishment answers for application forms. Select one entry by lane and job-description signals; never invent metrics, customers, revenue, adoption, pilots, or private details.

entries.name: Tenure
entries.status: LaunchNY cohort venture; pilot-ready; pre-pilot hardening
entries.answer: I built Tenure, a LaunchNY cohort venture and pilot-ready AI knowledge platform. It turns specialist knowledge into reviewed SOPs, a permissioned organizational wiki, cited Q&A, and process-intelligence reports; the measurable outcome is a shipped v1.1 product ready for pre-pilot hardening, without claiming customers or completed pilots.

entries.name: Quality Runner
entries.status: published PyPI v0.6.0 local-first Python CLI and MCP server
entries.answer: I built and published Quality Runner, a Python CLI and MCP server that compiles repository standards, detects available checks, normalizes evidence-backed findings, and writes ordered remediation plans. Its outcome is a reviewable, read-only quality workflow that gives engineers and agents structured evidence before source changes.

entries.name: AIOS
entries.status: working local-first operating layer and public case study
entries.answer: I built AIOS, a local-first operating layer for AI-assisted engineering. Session hooks capture events into SQLite, while a project-memory model separates raw automation artifacts from human-reviewed notes, making agent work reproducible and inspectable without claiming customer adoption.

entries.name: Pre-CR Suite
entries.status: published npm v0.1.0 package surface; public beta across VS Code, Neovim, and headless CLI
entries.answer: I built Pre-CR Suite, a TypeScript monorepo that gives VS Code, Neovim, and a headless CLI the same changed-line coverage workflow before code review. I centralized the behavior in a shared core package and LSP server, so clients do not drift into separate implementations.

entries.name: Terrace
entries.status: published npm v0.1.1 CLI; v0.2.0 release candidate on dev
entries.answer: I built and published Terrace, a Node CLI for spec-driven, test-governed AI-assisted development. It turns repository intent and quality gates into recoverable workflow state, and its JSON ship check can fail CI deterministically when a blocking gate is present.

entries.name: TMCP
entries.status: published v0.5.7 MCP/plugin distribution with stable and experimental workflows
entries.answer: I built TMCP, an MCP server that compiles scattered skills, rules, prompts, and evidence into task-specific packets. The result is a portable workflow layer with stable tool contracts plus clearly labeled experimental harvest and recommendation paths.

entries.name: Research Domain Writing
entries.status: published PyPI v0.1.0 package; v0.2.0 release candidate on dev
entries.answer: I published Research Domain Writing, an agent-first harness for research-grounded writing. It validates structured research packets, emits auditable prompt bundles, and carries evidence limits and confidence through technical, music, and basketball writing workflows.

entries.name: eslint-plugin-anti-slop
entries.status: published npm v0.5.0 ESLint plugin and quality-gate CLI
entries.answer: I authored and published an ESLint 9 plugin that catches product-quality failures such as placeholder copy, unjustified client components, weak empty states, arbitrary z-index values, and missing reduced-motion fallbacks. It also provides a CLI quality gate so these standards can run before merge.

entries.name: BidCamp
entries.status: live closed beta
entries.answer: I built BidCamp, a live closed-beta multi-tenant SaaS platform for MBE and MWBE firms navigating government contracting. It combines procurement intelligence, Claude-powered RFP analysis and drafting, CRM workflows, human-reviewed digests, tenant-scoped RLS, and scheduled data workers without claiming paid adoption or a completed customer cohort.

entries.name: CrimClock
entries.status: legal-time intelligence product build / reviewer preview
entries.answer: I built CrimClock, a legal-time intelligence platform that turns procedural timing rules into explainable calculation outputs. It exposes statutes, exclusions, tolling, calculation steps, and plain-language context while staying clearly framed as decision-support infrastructure rather than legal advice.

entries.name: Hoopscout
entries.status: private beta
entries.answer: I built Hoopscout, a private-beta recruiting-intelligence workflow for coach-specific athlete search and school-fit decisions. It combines deterministic fit weighting, ranked signals, messaging, transcript controls, and moderation boundaries; private users and private repository details stay undisclosed.

entries.name: RemodelVision
entries.status: working product build; incomplete flows disclosed
entries.answer: I built RemodelVision, a working AI remodeling visualization and rough-cost-estimation pipeline. I connected vision assessment, image transformation, model selection, authenticated project views, and persisted data in a Next.js product while explicitly leaving incomplete save flows and specialist agents disclosed.

entries.name: BBDSE / CourtIQ
entries.status: analytics suite with merged simulator/product lane; public hosting paused
entries.answer: I built BBDSE/CourtIQ, a basketball analytics and simulator suite that turns modeling into decision-support and user-facing product workflows. The public deployment is currently paused, so I describe the repository and product lane accurately rather than claiming an active public service.

entries.name: Dsci-proj
entries.status: reproducible survival-analysis pipeline and triage dashboard
entries.answer: I built Dsci-proj, a reproducible survival-analysis pipeline and Next.js triage dashboard that models GitHub issue-resolution risk. I paired the statistical workflow with fixture-backed UI tests, CI, and deployment automation so the analysis could be inspected as a working decision product.

entries.name: Fantasy
entries.status: local-first dynasty fantasy-football intelligence app
entries.answer: I built Fantasy, a local-first dynasty fantasy-football intelligence app with FastAPI, React/Vite, DuckDB, ingestion workflows, a trade engine, dashboards, and a draft room. The project demonstrates how I turn messy domain data into interactive decision-support tools.

entries.name: Soundscape
entries.status: full-stack music social platform
entries.answer: I built Soundscape, a full-stack music social platform spanning Next.js web, tRPC, Prisma, and Expo product surfaces. The project shows my ability to carry shared product and data contracts across web and mobile rather than stopping at a single prototype page.

entries.name: EliHealth
entries.status: private mobile-first health and recovery data product
entries.answer: I built EliHealth, a private mobile-first health and recovery data product with Expo, Supabase/PostgreSQL, Health Connect, lab imports, human verification, and explicit non-diagnostic boundaries. The important outcome is a privacy-conscious data architecture that treats uncertain health inputs as reviewable rather than silently authoritative.

entries.name: Dispatches from Cyberspace
entries.status: full-stack publishing platform
entries.answer: I built Dispatches from Cyberspace, a full-stack publishing platform with an API, Postgres, Clerk, role-based access, revisions, comments, feeds, content management, and cross-posting. It is a strong example of building durable product workflows around permissions and content state, not just a marketing surface.

entries.name: Book
entries.status: interactive reader with Postgres-backed admin and content workflow
entries.answer: I built Book, an interactive reader with chapter manifests, motion, audio, particles, Postgres-backed admin APIs, roles, and a content workflow. The project combines a polished reader experience with the operational systems needed to publish and manage the content behind it.

entries.name: Chiron's Forge
entries.status: live applied-AI product
entries.answer: I built Chiron's Forge, a live applied-AI product that runs multi-model research, synthesis, independent judging, and refinement into skills, reports, and Cursor rules. It demonstrates an evaluation-oriented AI workflow without claiming customer adoption beyond the public product surface.

entries.name: Framework Labs
entries.status: public software research lab; reasoning-core portfolio
entries.answer: I built Framework Labs as a public software research lab for reusable reasoning systems. Its public work separates durable cores from the products built around them, with Concordia presented in production at Chiron's Forge, Continuum at Tenure Systems, and Praxis still in development; I keep the answer at that public-safe level rather than inventing adoption metrics.

entries.name: Career-Ops
entries.status: private local career evidence and application command center
entries.answer: I built and maintain a local Career-Ops workflow that connects verified project proof to targeted job search: claim-safe public evidence, human-reviewed social variants, role-aware application artifacts, and guarded outreach. It keeps the source evidence and human approval boundary visible instead of treating generated copy or a queued role as a submitted application.

entries.name: Forward Automations
entries.status: CTO; active client and startup delivery work
entries.answer: As CTO of Forward Automations, I have taken ambiguous client problems from prototype to shipped software: a Cleveland Clinic clinical-coaching MVP in two weeks, architecture productivity software that increased operational output by about 400%, a stable live-event application in 11 days, and AI marketing automation that cut production timelines by about 90% and drove about 1.5M organic views for a startup.

entries.name: Deepr
entries.status: technical consultant work for an a16z portfolio company
entries.answer: As a technical consultant for Deepr, an a16z portfolio company, I built an AI-powered photo-carousel content-generation system and an inline coverage-vector tool that made test-coverage awareness visible during code review. The work combined applied AI product delivery with developer tooling in a real startup environment.

entries.name: Amazon hiring-insights analytics
entries.status: Amazon SDE internship evidence; details intentionally limited until backfilled
entries.answer: During my Amazon SDE internships, I built a data-analytics project that provided actionable hiring insights to business leaders and hiring managers, while also contributing to internal testing and pipeline capabilities across distributed-systems environments. I keep the answer at this level until the team, stack, and scale details are confirmed.

entries.name: Agent Eval Contract
entries.status: public PyPI v0.2.0 contract package; v0.3.0 release candidate on dev
entries.answer: I built Agent Eval Contract, a typed contract package for recording agent tasks, runs, scores, failures, and normalized external benchmark results. The outcome is a stable evidence boundary between experimental harnesses and downstream reporting instead of one-off result formats.

entries.name: Context Compiler Contract
entries.status: portable ESM validation package
entries.answer: I built Context Compiler Contract, a portable ESM validator for context-compiler results and routing manifests. It gives agent infrastructure a small, explicit contract for validating compiled context before downstream routing uses it.

entries.name: Video Pipeline
entries.status: Remotion-based video composition package
entries.answer: I built a Remotion-based video composition pipeline with a reusable core package, normalized render specifications, presets, and validation. It gives native-demo production a repeatable engineering surface instead of a collection of manually edited one-offs.

entries.name: Jakye portfolio
entries.status: public portfolio with project-truth synchronization
entries.answer: I built and maintain a portfolio surface that synchronizes public-safe project truth into current-work and proof surfaces. The useful outcome is a single, maintained destination where a recruiter can understand the work without opening private repositories or relying on stale project claims.

entries.name: Agent Eval Runtime
entries.status: standalone local eval runtime; first slice is report-only
entries.answer: I built Agent Eval Runtime, a standalone local runtime for eval runs, paired comparisons, model selection, harnesses, benchmarks, and corpus evidence. The first slice is intentionally report-only and keeps a zero-record state explicit instead of borrowing data from AIOS.

entries.name: AI Context Runtime
entries.status: standalone local context and session-intelligence runtime with report-only boundaries
entries.answer: I built AI Context Runtime, a standalone local runtime for context compilation, knowledge packets, handoffs, and report-only session intelligence. It keeps private evidence separate from AIOS and exports versioned signals for downstream consumers instead of exposing its database directly.

entries.name: AI Workflow Leverage
entries.status: evidence-bounded cross-repository leverage runtime with review-gated execution
entries.answer: I built AI Workflow Leverage, a local-first runtime for measuring cross-repository shipping leverage through bounded reproductions, review-gated execution, acceptance evidence, and redacted public projections. It fails closed around sandbox, provenance, merge, deployment, and publication boundaries rather than treating automation as proof.

entries.name: macctl
entries.status: command-first macOS control plane with owner-only transport and explicit blocked states
entries.answer: I built macctl, a command-first macOS control plane with an owner-only daemon, guarded GUI workflows, local receipts, and explicit accessibility, capture, and approval boundaries. Its release checks distinguish verified behavior from blocked daemon or permission evidence instead of claiming a GUI action happened without proof.

entries.name: Marketing Autoresearch
entries.status: evidence-bounded weekly SEO/AEO research loop with fail-closed publication controls
entries.answer: I built Marketing Autoresearch, an evidence-bounded weekly SEO/AEO research loop for owned product surfaces. It uses fixed prompts, source-freshness checks, shadow runs, and separate apply/verify gates so research can improve decisions without quietly publishing new claims.

entries.name: Relay
entries.status: private keyboard-first native macOS workbench for local AI coding workflows
entries.answer: I built Relay, a private keyboard-first native macOS workbench for local AI coding workflows. It combines local session discovery, Playbook intelligence, derived Usage metrics, and guarded file transactions without requiring a Relay-operated backend or applying changes without explicit confirmation.
